stem: A Massachusetts prescription for Vyvanse contains no valid no-substitution direction. A lower-cost interchangeable product is listed, but neither the pharmacy nor its usual wholesaler can supply that product today. Which fact is most important to the interchange decision?

choices.text: The pharmacist must delay every prescription until the least expensive listed product can be obtained, regardless of availability.
The interchange mandate depends on a less expensive interchangeable product being reasonably available, so actual availability is material.
Schedule II status automatically prohibits use of any interchangeable product in Massachusetts.
The pharmacist must choose the product with the highest acquisition cost whenever a listed product is out of stock.
The prescription becomes invalid because the wholesaler cannot supply the less expensive product that day.

explanation.core_reasoning: Massachusetts does not describe the default merely as ‘use any listed generic.’ The statutory pathway refers to a less expensive, reasonably available interchangeable product. When the lower-cost product is not reasonably available, that prerequisite becomes the key fact.

choice_analysis.A: The law’s use of reasonable availability matters; it does not require an indefinite delay for an unavailable product.
choice_analysis.B: This identifies the availability element built into the Massachusetts interchange default.
choice_analysis.C: Lisdexamfetamine’s Schedule II status does not itself create a blanket no-interchange rule.
choice_analysis.D: Higher acquisition cost is not the statutory substitute for the reasonable-availability analysis.
choice_analysis.E: A supply problem with one interchangeable product does not by itself invalidate an otherwise valid prescription.

related_facts: The prescriber’s valid no-substitution direction is a separate way the default can change.
Controlled-substance scheduling and product interchange answer different legal questions.
explanation.mpje_trap: The word ‘interchangeable’ is not enough; ask whether the qualifying lower-cost product is reasonably available.

reasoning_steps: Confirm there is no valid no-substitution direction
Identify reasonable availability as a required part of the ordinary interchange pathway
